Ozempic

By: Julian Sun | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Ozempic: Miracle Drug to fight obesity or dangerous quick fix?

Unique Selling Point:
We look at the ozempic craze sweeping the world and its impact in South Africa. Touted as a miracle drug to combat obesity and endorsed by international celebrities and social-media influencers has seen demand for Ozempic exceed supply. We get to the bottom of how it works and uncover an illicit market for fake versions on the drug being pedalled on-line.

Summary:
There's an obesity epidemic sweeping the world, including South Africa, with over 20 million South African adults struggling with being overweight or obese, with women comprising 68% of this group.

Now the miracle drug Ozempic offers a potential solution to what is fast becoming the most serious health crisis facing South Africa. Already Type 2 Diabetes is the leading cause of death in South African women.

In this story, we will explain how Ozempic works, and its meteoric rise to public consciousness. We will meet people who have experienced tremendous benefits of taking the drug, look at the negative side effects that could arise and highlight a growing market of illicit ozempic being sold illegally online and how easy it is to buy.

Extra Budget Items:
R&D budget to buy some of the illicit "fake ozempic" being sold online in South Africa

Script:


OZEMPIC




V/O
It’s known as “the darling shot of Hollywood”. Injectable prescription medicine, hailed by celebrities as the holy grail of weight loss. And everyone, it seems, is scrambling to get their hands on it.


It’s called… Ozempic
UPS
[Advert snippet]
V/O
Developed and registered to treat type 2 diabetes and the associated risks of heart disease, over the past few years Ozempic, and other similar drugs have become gamechangers for many.
Natalie
no matter how hard I'm trying with diet, with exercise, with following all the advice that I'm doing, I'm just not getting into the non dangerous levels of my blood sugar readings. [00:06:02][23.8]


V/O
Natalie Horn is a type 2 diabetic, struggling to control her blood sugar levels. Three years ago her doctor suggested she look into a new course of treatment – Injections to help regulate sugar levels and the production of insulin in her body.
Natalie
We ended up going with, a brand called Trulicity. And within weeks my sugar went from about. The 8 to 10 range right down to five and a half six range, still doing exactly what I'd been doing before, so it was incredibly effective for my sugar levels,


V/O
Trulicity and Ozempic – and others like Mounjaro and Saxenda – are part of a class of drugs known as GLP-1 agonists. They are all similar, but work with different active ingredients… and some patients respond better to certain products…


Natalie
Natalie: [00:10:04] So with being on Trulicity at that point and I could immediately feel the health benefits. At that stage, we were running a restaurant. So you running on your feet all day will not. My energy levels shot up as I was losing the weight. Mentally, it was such a huge weight. Not just a physical weight, but a mental weight of me knowing that I'm treating my body better.
V/O
Ozempic is a synthetic drug inspired by the venomous saliva of a native American reptile, called the Gila monster. These giant lizards can go for long periods without eating because of a specific hormone that’s similar to the GLP hormone in humans.
Dr May
So, when you’re hungry there’s hormones in your stomach that will go up and say seek food. Once you’ve got food and the calories are now moving down the bowel you need something to stop, and say okay we’ve eaten enough and now we’re done. GLP is one of those signalling hormones that will say now we’ve hit satiety.
V/O
Endocrinologist, Dr Wayne May explains that Ozempic and other GLP-1 agonists mimic that natural hormone; making you less hungry and fuller for longer. And of course that leads to significant weight loss for most patients.
Dr May
Ozempic will lose you on average 15% of your body weight, which is 3 times what we were looking at before. And on occasions you get some super-responders who might even lose 20, 25, 30% body weight.
V/O
And this is what all the fuss is about. Finally, a weight-loss drug that really works.
UPS Social Media


V/O
The demand for drugs like Ozempic has skyrocketed and the manufacturers simply can’t keep up.
Natalie
Natalie: [00:07:38] But within six months of me starting on trulicity, all of a sudden, it just all of it trulicity ozempic anything like that just wasn't available, from pharmacies anymore. [00:07:51][12.8]
V/O
Novo Nordisk – the Danish company that manufactures Ozempic sold more than 30 billion US dollars’ worth of diabetic and obesity drugs in 2023. But the world wants more and those who need it are struggling to get it.
Dr May
The issue where it’s gone wrong is that the wrong people use it, the ones that are just slightly overweight and they shouldn’t be using it… This is to treat excess weight and associated co-morbidities.
V/O
GLP-1 agonists are NOT meant for cosmetic weight loss, even though thousands of people are turning to these drugs.
The true value of these medicines is in the treatment of obesity.
Tasneem
I weighed 122 kilos, which is the highest that I’ve ever weighed in my entire life.
V/O


Tasneem Alexander has always struggled with her weight.
Tasneem
Covid was one of the worst things that could have happened to me in terms of my health because not only did I not have access to people that saw me, that would say, Tasneem, something is not okay, But also you were at home, you were not exercising properly and I think it’s the banana bread pandemic.
Claire: Right I remember.
V/O
Post-pandemic Tasneem tried to turn her health around.. She changed her diet, started exercising, but with little success.
In 2022 she consulted Dr May and he prescribed Ozempic.
Dr May
Claire: Why was Ozempic the right choice for her?
Dr May: In terms of Tasneem she had a markedly high BMI sitting at about 40. Along with that she also had comorbidities. She had PCOS, she was pre-diabetes and she had asthma as well.
V/O
But medical intervention, especially when it comes to obesity, has always raised eyebrows.
Hassina Kajee
Throwing a pill at somebody that is going to use one mechanism to help them lose weight doesn’t answer the question “why did they gain weight in the first place”.
V/O
Dr Hassina Kajee heads the Nutrition Network and is an advocate for the Low-carb/High-fat diet… Like many others she questions the widespread use of GLP-1 agonists.
Hassina Kajee
[00:06:43] It's a quick fix. Pharmaceuticals is not going to be the answer to a disease that is caused by lifestyle. It should be the reversal of whatever caused that problem.
V/O
Longtime activist for equitable access to HIV treatments, Prof Francois Venter, says the current debates around GLP-1 agonists are similar to those around antiretrovirals in the 1990’s.
Francois Venter
These new drugs are not just game-changers, they’re life changers. So people who have established obesity and who’ve gained weight, it’s next to impossible to shift without chemical help. That’s the sad reality.
Francois Venter
Claire: There’s so much stigma around weight gain and obesity. A lot of people think, well you gained the weight through eating, isn’t that a choice. You should be making better decisions about your life.
Francois: It’s almost a moral judgement on people for gaining weight. Which is very similar to the HIV field; you don’t blame the person for having HIV you talk about the forces around it, you know and the same with obesity. Obesity experts don’t talk like that. They say you’re putting on weight because your environment coupled with your genetics with whatever is going on.
V/O
Over 50% of adults in South Africa are classified as obese and while poor diet and lifestyle choices play a role, it is far more complicated than that.
Francois Venter
You have all sorts of body mechanisms and physiology that says we’re not going to let you go, it feels like you’re starving and you will shut down all sorts of parts of your body to try and conserve that weight.
V/O
Besides often fighting their own genetics, many obese patients don’t necessarily have the luxury of choice.
Francois Venter
Poor people are particularly predisposed towards having obesity because they have less choices that are forces upon them…
V/O
And at the moment the option of using medicine like Ozempic does not come cheap… A month’s supply will cost anything from R2000 to R5000 rand, depending on the brand.
Francois
People are desperate and they’re willing to do almost everything for these drugs. Watching the exploitation, not just from the drug manufacturers who make the drugs, but also from people selling counterfeit drugs is disgusting.
Dr May
When anything is in high demand and it’s not available then everybody who’s got a plot and a scheme comes out of the woodwork. So, now what’s happened is there’s people who are cooking it up in different places. We don’t know what’s in those medications, I don’t know what’s in them. I don’t know what the doses are. And if I don’t know what I’m giving to a patent and if you get a side-effect I don’t know what you’re having a side-effect to or reaction to.
Natalie Horn
I’m still phoning pharmacies, and I’m looking online and I’m seeing online people selling ozempic-type of injections, and I’m mortified, because you don’t know what’s inside these things… but I’ll tell you, I was tempted.
V/O
But it’s not just counterfeits that pose health risks…
Even the real deal comes with side-effects.
Kajee



So there are key studies showing the risks of these drugs. You know, one of the most common ones being nausea, vomiting, digestive issues. They’re quite catastrophic in many cases. There are others that show the risk associated with types of cancers like pancreatic cancers.
Francois
There are often gastro-intestinal side-effects, which can be a little bit unpleasant. Most of the side-effects are simply annoying rather than life-threatening or even serious.
V/O
The debates around the use and purpose of drugs like Ozempic keep raging, but the fact is; in the right hands, and with proper medical oversight… these medicines are effective and are changing lives…
Francois Venter
This is not simply a cosmetic thing where people lose weight. People lose weight, your blood pressure comes down, all your metabolic parameters get better, there’s less strokes, less heart failure, less kidney disease, less liver disease… people need access to this for their health, not just to make themselves look better.


*** END
PROMO 1 21”
Millions of South Africans are overweight despite having tried every diet under the sun.
UPS FRANCOIS
Eating properly is very very important for your health. We also now know that being active is even more important than we ever appreciated before. Neither one of them, though, is a good way to lose weight.
But is the answer injectable prescription medicines like Ozempic?
PROMO 2 21”
When it comes to weight loss… Ozempic and similar medicines have taken the world by storm.
UPS Dr May: Ozempic will lose you on average 15% of your body weight, which is 3 times what we were looking at before.
But is this the solution for the growing obesity epidemic?
PROMO 3 21”
What do the Gila monster… prescription medication, and influencers across the globe have in common?
UPS: Tasneem: it’s really truly changed my life in every aspect.
UPS Francois: These new drugs are not just game-changers, they’re life changers.
